i226-lm.note: The only port with AMT. A host OS that bridges it or changes its MAC kills out-of-band access without touching anything that looks related.

i226-v.note: No AMT. Identical-looking socket next to the one that has it.

sfp28-1.note: Ubuntu names it for the X710's second function, and sfp28-2 for its first: LLDP on the ToRs showed ber1-edge's and ber1-svc's sfp28-1 DACs arriving from enp2s0f1np1 (2026-09-24).

appliance.note: A KVM, a PDU or a transfer-switch card: one network port, and management is all it does.

mgmt.note: Its only port, so unlike an MS-01 there is no identical socket next to it to get wrong.

mac-mini.note: Apple silicon has no BMC and no AMT, so this hardware has no out-of-band network path at all. Recovery is a PDU outlet cycle plus `pmset autorestart 1`, and its console is a crash-cart KVM wheeled to the box rather than a permanent link. That is why it declares no out-of-band interface: the absence is the fact, and it is what makes the switched PDU a recovery dependency rather than a convenience.

en0.note: Its only NIC, so a mini lands on exactly one ToR.

eats16n.note: 1U, 2x C20 in, 8x C13 plus 1x C19 out, 16A/3.84kW, 8 ms transfer. Networking is built in (Netpack). Its card is taken to be a Network-M2, which serves the REST API the PDUs speak (/rest/mbdetnrs), and that is what the RackATS controller targets; the same card serves the EATON-ATS2-MIB over SNMP once SNMP is enabled, which it is not from the factory. Source 1 is feed A, source 2 feed B.

netpack.note: Built-in management network port. Eaton's Netpack, not an add-in card.

source-1.note: C20 inlet for source 1, feed A.

source-2.note: C20 inlet for source 2, feed B.

evmafc20a.note: Switched zero-U PDU. Speaks Modbus TCP, a REST API, SNMP, LDAP and HTTPS; the REST API is what a power driver should target. This is the remote-power path the Mac fleet's recovery model depends on, because a mini has no out-of-band of its own.

sensor.note: The SENSOR port: feeds and powers the RS485 (Modbus) chain of environmental probes, which run probe to probe over RJ45 cables.

outlets.sockets: Odd outlets C13, even outlets hybrid C13/C19, so every outlet takes a C14 plug and the even ones a C20 too.

emp-gen2.note: No Ethernet at all. It hangs off a PDU's SENSOR port over an RJ45 cable carrying RS485 (Modbus), chained probe to probe, and draws its power over that link, so it occupies no switch port and has no management link. Its identity on the bus is a Modbus address, not a NIC.

rs501a-e12.note: Rack 2's edge and storage server. Interface names and MACs as the bench unit (TAS0CG000177) reported them on Ubuntu 24.04. Its BMC is adopted over Redfish (infra/rack-nodes).

bmc.note: The leftmost of the three RJ45 ports on the back: the BMC's dedicated port.

lan1.note: The middle RJ45, the first onboard port: cabled to its ToR's management port for the ToR's zero-touch provisioning. The BMC's NC-SI sideband also rides it: a switch on this port learned the BMC's second MAC there.

n225p-1.note: Broadcom N225P port 1. Linked at 10G with FEC off on a 10G SFP+ DAC; 25G needs an SFP28 DAC into the ToR's SFP28 ports. An admin-down port keeps its link, so a bond on it runs fast LACP. Its rings hold at most 2047 descriptors (ethtool -g, measured 26 Oct).
